standard_prerequisites: The scheme-level base change criterion of Derived Categories of Schemes cited in the statement
Derived pullback to the small etale site and the strict henselization description of stalks of quasi-coherent complexes on algebraic spaces
Faithful flatness of the map from a local ring to its strict henselization, and the Tor-comparison lemma for strict henselizations of fibre products
core_obligations: Show the pointwise base change condition (1) is etale local on X'
Pull back the given map on the small etale sites of scheme presentations and compare condition (1) of this lemma with condition (1) of the scheme-level lemma
Prove the top arrow of the stalk diagram is the base change of the bottom arrow, using faithful flatness of local rings into strict henselizations

Verify the commutation of cohomology of derived tensor products under strict henselization via the cited Tor comparison lemma, whose flatness hypotheses hold by the functorial strict henselization identification
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the scheme case using the comparison lemma for the derived categories of the small etale sites
Write stalks of K and K' as derived tensor products with strict henselizations
Arrange the commutative square of cohomology groups and check the top horizontal map is obtained from the bottom one by the faithfully flat base change O_{X',x'} to O_{X',x'barn}
Conclude the equivalence of isomorphism by faithful flatness, quoting the Tor comparison lemma and verifying its flatness hypotheses
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is an etale descent statement for the pointwise base change isomorphism condition on a cartesian square of algebraic spaces (source lines 5364-5485, label lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition). The solver must transport the condition between the small etale site and scheme presentations, express stalks through strict henselizations, and prove that the cohomology comparison arrow is a faithfully flat base change of the scheme-level arrow, which requires the Tor comparison lemma and a check of its flatness hypotheses; the bookkeeping across four spaces and two derived tensor products is substantive. Allowed background: the cited scheme lemma and the henselization lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
